Mao Zedong (also spelled **Mao Tse‑tung**) was a Chinese revolutionary leader who became one of the most influential figures in modern history. | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Birth / Death** | Born December 26, 1893; died September 9, 1976. | | **Early Life & Education** | Grew up in Shaoshan, Hunan Province. Studied at the National University of Peking (now Tsinghua). Became involved in leftist politics during his student years. | | **Political Rise** | Joined the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 1921. Played key roles in early party organization, especially after the split between communists and nationalists (Kuomintang). Led guerrilla forces against Japanese invasion during WWII. | | **Founding of PRC** | Declared the founding of the People’s Republic of China on October 1, 1949, becoming its first Chairman. | | **Key Policies/Initiatives** | • *Land Reform* – redistributed land from landlords to peasants.
• *First Five-Year Plan* – industrialization push.
• *Great Leap Forward* (1958–1962) – aimed at rapid collectivization and industrial output but led to famine.
• *Cultural Revolution* (1966–1976) – radical social campaign targeting perceived “capitalist” elements, causing widespread upheaval. | | **Leadership Style** | Charismatic yet authoritarian. Emphasized mass mobilization, ideological purity, and centralized control. | | **Legacy** | • Modernized parts of China’s economy and infrastructure.
• Created a unified nation-state under communist rule.
• Responsible for millions of deaths due to policy failures (especially Great Leap Forward and Cultural Revolution).
• Remains a polarizing figure—admired for anti-imperialist stance and criticized for human rights abuses. | He remains a central symbol in discussions of 20th-century geopolitics, socialism, and China's development trajectory.
